newsitem.title: MEXICO: Schlumberger-led group wins Mexico drilling bid.
newsitem.headline: Schlumberger-led group wins Mexico drilling bid.

text.p: A consortia of companies led by Schlumberger Ltd. won bidding for a natural gas drilling project in Mexico's Burgos Basin, state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) director Adrian Lajous said on Thursday in a statement.
The French company was joined in the bid by Perforadora Mexico and Compania Mexicana de Exploraciones, Pemex said.

"The three companies that got the first integral service contract will be in charge of drilling 31 wells in the Arcabuz-Culebra field, with an approximate depth of between 2,650 and 2,950 meters each," Pemex said.

Drilling will require "extensive 3-D seismic surveys, the adoption of new drilling and fracturing techniques and improved engineering quality," Lajous has said. A later service contact will be auctioned after July.

Seven companies submitted bids for the mammoth Tamaulipas state drilling project near the Texas border, company sources said. TransTexas Gas Corp., Halliburton Co., Empresas ICA, Protexa, BJ Services Co. and Perforadora Campeche were competing bidders.

Burgos Basin is Mexico's largest source of non-associated gas, gas extracted alone and not with crude oil. The drilling project is part of a three-prong effort in 1997 to accelerate the company's petroleum output.
